newsitem.title: USA: E. Corn Belt to warm up after wet, cool weekend.
newsitem.headline: E. Corn Belt to warm up after wet, cool weekend.

text.p: Fledgling corn and soybean crops in the Eastern Corn Belt face another weekend of rains and cool temperatures but the outlook for early next week is warmer and drier, meteorologists said.

Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express Inc, said eastern Iowa, Illinois and states such as Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky would receive "rains of 0.5 to 1.5 inches locally heavier with 80 percent coverage" over the weekend.
High temperatures will be in the 60s Fahrenheit in that region and the wettest areas (north-central Kentucky and southern Indiana) could have at least four inches of rain.
But he noted the weather should change early next week.

"The entire corn belt should be dry late Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday with next front due in Thursday," Gesser of Weather Express said, noting highs in that period should be in the upper 70s and low 80s F.
Further west (Nebraska, western Iowa, the Dakotas) the weather should be "high and dry" this weekend with temperatures in the upper 70s and low 80s F, Gesser said.
Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp, also expected widespread rains of 0.50 to 1.50 inches in the Eastern Corn Belt this weekend with below normal temperatures.
He forecast conditions should warm up next week although the next rain bearing system should bring wetter, cooler weather back to the Eastern Corn Belt, possibly on Thursday.
Further south in Texas, where the hard red winter wheat crop is currently being harvested, some weekend showers could disrupt combining, meteorologists said.
"The bottom line is there are going to be showers," Gesser of Weather Express said, noting rain had already arrived in west-central Texas from Midland through Lubbock.
Rain should cover 20 to 30 percent of the state Saturday with similar coverage Sunday and Monday, he added.
WSC's Burgio said a few weekend showers were possible but it was "nothing to really impede harvest activity."
He forecast scattered showers and possible thunderstorms Monday through Thursday with total of 0.30 to 1.00 inch, locally heavier for the period.
